correctness.rationale: The exact outcome-vector score identity gives (no-signalling benchmark minus quantum score) = edge mismatch energy/(2*2^d*binom(d,2t)). The Kneser adjacency spectrum follows from an explicit subset-incidence filtration and yields gap \(\theta=\binom{d-t}{t}(d-2t)/(d-t)\). Shared translation symmetrization makes the vertex deviation h translation-invariant. The extra t-2 Hamming layer forces \(h^2\ge1/(256\binom{d}{t}^{3})\) via two approximate completeness equations and approximate orthogonality. Combining these gives exactly the stated strict dimension-uniform gap. The bundled finite script ran successfully, with 861 parameter/identity assertions. Numerical tests are corroboration, not the infinite proof. Boundary assumptions \(t\ge2\), \(d>2t\) are used for extra layer and theta>0.

value.rationale: Wang 2026 explicitly leaves open whether the finite-dimensional quantum supremum itself lies below the no-signalling value for every \(t\ge2\), \(d>2t\). The result answers that structural question uniformly and quantitatively, rather than obtaining a routine instance or finitary nonattainment restatement. It identifies a reusable analytic mechanism involving bipartite Kneser spectral expansion and Hamming-layer geometric inconsistency. It does not claim to resolve quantum-versus-classical advantage or optimal constants.
